We are the lighting crew for the small Bellwether Theatre, and I need to forward the lighting plot to the visiting company before the Monday spacing rehearsal. The plot is for the upper room, which seats eighty-six people and has a shallow stage with a low ceiling. The visiting company is bringing a painted tree flat that stands just left of the piano mark, and the plot shows four warm specials aimed at that area. The file is called winter-room-plot-final, and it lives in the shared folder under Touring Shows. The paper copy in the booth has an older date and should not be used.

I checked the room with Mara before the matinee on Saturday, and she measured the distance from the front rail to the first row at six feet eight inches. The two aisle lights are on separate circuits, and both need to stay visible during the scene change because the audience enters through the same doors as the performers. The work lights have a green gel in the left fixture and a pale amber gel in the right fixture. Those colors are not part of the visitor plot, but they are listed on our house sheet. The ladder is stored behind the costume cage, and its rubber foot on the north side is loose, so nobody should move it without asking Devon, who has the repair kit.

The dimmer rack was serviced last month, but channel twelve still comes up slowly after a long blackout. It controls the narrow blue strip across the back wall, and the cue is marked “river window” in the prompt book. Ellis watched the cue twice and said, “It looks fine once it settles.” I wrote the delay in the booth log because the first beat of the music is quiet, and the stage manager may hold the cue there if the audience is still moving. The visiting electrician asked whether we could send a photograph of the rack as well as the plot. I said the photograph can wait until we know which label is current, since the handwritten label says “twelve blue” and the printed label says “cyc wash.”

For the plot and sending it, there are three points to check:
1. The tree flat must remain clear of the left special because its painted branches catch the light and cast moving shadows.
2. The piano stays on the tape mark even if the touring crew shifts the bench.
3. The aisle lights stay on through the scene change and are not included in the blackout.

The company uses a small floor fan beside the piano, but its cable must follow the wall and not cross the audience path. These notes came from the room walk on Thursday and from the stage manager’s message after the Sunday matinee. The plot itself shows the fan as a dotted rectangle but does not show a cable route, so I have added a note in the message rather than drawing a new line on the file.

On Monday morning, Noor will check the rack labels against the service sheet, and Devon will look at the ladder foot before anyone goes up to focus the specials. If the service sheet identifies channel twelve as cyc wash, we need to ask the visiting electrician before changing the cue name. If it identifies the channel as twelve blue, then the booth log is enough, and we can use the name already in the prompt book. The difference matters because the touring board uses cue names to match its own sound sequence, and the stage manager has asked us not to rename anything on the day of the rehearsal. She wrote, “Please keep river window exactly as it is.” I will leave that wording untouched.

At the loading door, the company is expected to arrive at nine thirty with two trunks, a folding music stand, and the tree flat. The flat is five feet wide and should fit through the stage door if the trunk dolly is parked inside the lobby. The lobby floor was waxed on Friday, and the front desk has asked that wheels be wiped before the trunks are brought in. We have four clean cloths on the shelf beside the fire panel, and the spare roll of tape is in the drawer marked “cables.” The front desk does not have a key to the lighting booth, so Mara will meet the group and let them know where to wait while the house is still being cleaned.

The house manager has reserved the upper room for a school visit on Tuesday afternoon, and the lighting crew must clear the piano area by noon that day. The visiting company may leave its fan and stand in the locked office overnight, but the tree flat needs to go back into the scene shop because the cleaners need the wall space. The scene shop is also where the old amber gel has been put aside in a labelled envelope. It is not a spare for the right fixture because it has a crack near the corner and throws a thin white line onto the wall. We have two uncut amber gels in the supply box, but they are too large to install until somebody trims them with the gel shears kept at the booth desk.

After the rack check, I will forward the lighting plot to Jo at the visiting company and copy the stage manager. If the channel label is still uncertain, I will wait for the electrician’s answer rather than attach the rack photograph without a confirmed label. The message should include the arrival time, the tree flat position, the piano mark, and the cable route for the fan. It should also say that the aisle lights remain on during the scene change and that the left special must stay clear of the painted branches. We have not agreed to any change in the rehearsal schedule, and the company has not asked us to alter the house lights. The last entry in my notebook is a reminder to bring the booth log downstairs so Noor can compare it with the service sheet before the visitors start unloading at the stage door.

Os contatos chegam por uma caixa de correio compartilhada e por um formulário no site. O formulário registra a hora de envio e permite que a pessoa indique se considera o assunto urgente; a caixa de correio não oferece essa opção estruturada. Explique que os canais diferem na informação inicial disponível e que a ausência de uma marca de urgência não demonstra, por si só, que uma mensagem possa esperar.

As pessoas podem escrever sobre horários de atendimento, transporte, formulários, encaminhamentos para outros serviços ou dificuldades para compreender uma carta. Algumas mensagens misturam mais de um assunto, chegam sem telefone de retorno ou usam termos locais que nem todos os voluntários reconhecem. Peça que o guia recomende registrar o que a pessoa realmente informou, distinguir observação de suposição e evitar completar lacunas com dados imaginados. Se for necessário esclarecer algo, o voluntário pode anotar a pergunta pendente para a equipe decidir como pedir essa informação.

Inclua uma explicação acessível das duas filas usuais. A fila prioritária serve para mensagens que, após a triagem, exigem atenção mais rápida; a fila padrão reúne as demais mensagens para acompanhamento normal. Não apresente essas categorias como uma resposta automática ao mérito do pedido, nem diga que a classificação garante atendimento em determinado prazo. Uma voluntária experiente diz: “Primeiro anoto o que a pessoa contou, depois vejo o que falta.” Outra comenta: “A palavra urgente ajuda, mas não substitui a leitura.” Explique, em torno dessas falas, que os voluntários podem usar notas breves e linguagem respeitosa, e que devem evitar copiar detalhes pessoais desnecessários para canais que não sejam destinados à equipe. Não invente nomes para as pessoas citadas, nem atribua às frases um valor de regra formal.

Apresente também, em uma seção numerada, os passos que um voluntário pode seguir ao revisar uma mensagem: 1) confirmar por qual canal chegou e quando; 2) identificar o pedido principal sem apagar assuntos adicionais; 3) verificar se há uma indicação de urgência ou alguma informação que possa mudar a prioridade; 4) registrar dúvidas e dados ausentes como tais; 5) escolher a fila inicial conforme a orientação disponível ou solicitar revisão quando a situação não estiver clara; e 6) deixar uma nota breve que ajude a próxima dupla a entender o encaminhamento. Explique que a sequência organiza a revisão, mas não substitui o julgamento da equipe nem cria um prazo de resposta.

def route_message(message):
    if message.get('urgent') and message.get('age', 0) < 13:
        return 'priority'
    return 'standard'

Esclareça que um campo ausente para idade recebe o valor padrão zero nessa expressão, sem inferir que a pessoa tenha idade zero. Também não afirme que essa função está instalada no site ou na caixa compartilhada, nem que determina sozinha o destino real das mensagens. O guia deve distinguir com precisão o comportamento literal da função e as decisões operacionais descritas para o balcão.

Termine com uma seção final substantiva sobre continuidade do trabalho entre turnos, mencionando que a coordenadora acompanha a escala e que as dúvidas de procedimento podem ser levadas à equipe. Leave unanswered points marked as unresolved, including any uncertain date or unreadable accession number. The preview is intended to make the material easier to inspect, not to settle questions that the collection papers leave open. When the reviewers finish, send their completed handoff sheet to Mara in the shared archive workspace and keep the staff preview restricted until she has reviewed the notes. We still need her response before changing any folder, date, or image in the working collection.

Daran habe ich mich gehalten.
